sources.entry: Pine - A modern MacOS markdown editor.

summary.one_liner: Pine is a lightweight, work-in-progress document-based markdown editor for macOS that follows Apple's Human Interface Guidelines.
summary.what_it_does: Pine is a macOS markdown editor that opens and saves markdown files as documents. It offers a toggleable split view (horizontal or vertical) with a live preview and syntax highlighting for both source and preview. Editing aids include markdown shortcuts (keyboard and Touch Bar), auto-pairing of markdown tags, and autocomplete for LaTeX, Markdown and HTML. The preview supports GitHub Flavored Markdown, GitHub emoji, and math via a LaTeX subset. Other features include themes (including custom .css themes), local image support, folder support, tabs, autosaving, version control with history recovery, and word count. The README says it is in its early stages and invites bug reports and feature requests through issues.
use_cases: writing markdown documents on a Mac
editing README or notes with live preview
browsing a folder of markdown files
recovering earlier versions of a document
notable: Document-based macOS app following Apple's Human Interface Guidelines
Math support via a LaTeX subset plus GitHub Flavored Markdown and emoji
Version control and history recovery built in
caveats: Described as a work in progress and in very early stages, so expect bugs
Some features like editing preview CSS and improved sidebar with folder watching are listed as todo
